issue.description:
Slice 2 of 4 of the beadrs-40f0cc4e auto-split. Depends on slice 1 (out-of-band-change fixtures in tests/checkpoint_set_v2_conformance.rs).

Scope: root-cause and fix the covered-ahead superset refusal that makes set-v2-shard-merge-on-deletion red. Recorded leads from the prior attempt — do not re-derive: verify_superset (src/service/reconcile.rs:380) compares read_all_events(conn) against stage_set_v2_checkpoint output; staging reads only manifest-referenced rows, so injected orphans never enter it; suspects are wire-identity re-derivation (local_identity_basis / derive_wire_identity) or detail/actor normalization in process_checkpoint_file event parsing diverging after an out-of-band store change.

Acceptance:
- set-v2-shard-merge-on-deletion passes (via the slice-1 fixtures where applicable).
- The six previously-green scenarios stay green in the same scoped run.
- The root cause is recorded on the bead (which lead it was, or what else it turned out to be).
- fmt and clippy clean for the touched targets, measured from a git-archive extraction of the branch HEAD with a private target dir under /build/bead-rs/ and a fresh TMPDIR outside the extraction — the shared checkout carries another bead's uncommitted WIP (build.rs, src/main.rs, src/service/git.rs, src/service/doctor.rs, src/service/checkpoint/sync_resolve.rs, tests/build_from_archive_checkout_untouched.rs, tests/needle_variant_dispatch_paths.rs) that does not clippy-compile; never measure or fix rival WIP.

Out of scope: crash-ordering specifics (slice 3), reader/migration/restore, redaction tooling (beadrs-4c81a20f).
issue.notes:
ROOT CAUSE (recorded per acceptance; which lead it was): neither recorded suspect — it was the missing third mechanism. Out-of-band `DELETE FROM issues` CASCADES to events (schema: events.issue_id REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; the test's bundled rusqlite defaults foreign_keys ON), so the live store loses its newest event rows and MAX(sequence) drops BELOW the pointer's snapshot_sequence. classify() then computes covered > live => remote-advanced and runs verify_superset, where read_all_events' positional wire-identity derivation (NULL-origin rows numbered 1..N in scan order via local_identity_basis/derive_wire_identity) renumbers every survivor after the first gap, so live identity (uuid,5) names a different event than the staged segment's (uuid,5) => "different content" => covered-ahead integrity failure, flush refused. The wire-identity derivation itself is R027-spec'd and left unchanged.

FIX (2 production files + 1 message file):
- src/service/reconcile.rs classify: the recorded-generation fast path no longer requires covered <= live. A pointer whose exact generation_id + root hash + covered sequence match checkpoint_state is the local publisher's own output for ANY covered/live relation (spec remote-advanced-reconcile-v1: "a locally recorded generation, its recorded generation, sequence and root hash authenticate the previously published prefix"; a pull by construction leaves checkpoint_state naming a different generation). covered > live there means the store lost rows its own publication covered — local housekeeping repairable by flush — so it reports Behind (the republish remedy), never remote-advanced, whose guard would wedge every mutation against the workspace's own last publication.
- src/service/checkpoint.rs forensic_checkpoint_status_inner: dirty := covered != live (was covered < live), so the flush-only idempotent short-circuit no longer swallows the republish that repairs an out-of-band-shrunken store.
- src/service/git_commit.rs: dirty-refusal message inequality corrected (< -> !=) for the new reachable direction.

TESTS:
- tests/r027_remote_advanced_reconcile.rs: new recorded_generation_republishes_after_out_of_band_event_loss pins the taxonomy (behind + dirty after cascade loss; explicit flush republishes a new generation; guard stays writable).
- tests/checkpoint_set_v2_conformance.rs set-v2-shard-merge-on-deletion: the final retention assertion was unsatisfiable as written — after split-then-merge, consecutive generations share almost no shard files, so `on_disk <= current_rows + 2` contradicts spec 7.3's two-generation retention (the 15 split children are exactly one generation old, retained via previous.json). Replaced with what 7.3 actually promises: (a) containment — nothing on disk outside current∪previous manifests; (b) after one real mutation+flush slides the window, the split children are reaped and the original boundedness holds. Probe-verified before edit: post-merge on-disk = 30 files = exactly the two-generation union, orphans 0.
